risks.risk: Alert fatigue from false positives erodes trust in alerts
risks.mitigation: 2-of-3 detector vote, dollar severity tiers, planned-event suppression (B17) before Slack goes live

risks.risk: Billing data latency (24-72h) and late restatements delay or distort detection
risks.mitigation: Score only finalised days, re-run on restated data, alert only on upward moves

risks.risk: Poor tag hygiene limits attribution below the account/service level
risks.mitigation: Attribute on account and service first (no tags needed); add a tag-coverage KPI before team-level rollups

risks.risk: Synthetic data overstates real-world detection accuracy
risks.mitigation: Multi-seed robustness check, results labelled as synthetic, validate on a FOCUS-format export before any claim

risks.risk: Seasonal baseline breaks on structural changes (migrations, commitment purchases)
risks.mitigation: Trailing-median level adapts in about two weeks; add change-point reset in the forecast milestone

risks.risk: Credits, refunds and amortised commitments distort daily cost
risks.mitigation: Use amortised net cost and exclude credit line items when real exports are loaded

risks.risk: LLM executive summary drifts from computed facts
risks.mitigation: Facts-only prompt, word-count guard and deterministic fallback; LLM is optional

data_insights: Analysed 365 days of synthetic spend across 3 providers and 54 series ($15,243,719 total, $41,764 per day).
The ensemble flagged 14 events: precision 0.93, recall 1.00, F1 0.96 against 12 injected anomalies; none missed.
Largest event E05 (2025-05-07 to 2025-05-20) carried $15,016 excess, driven by AWS S3 in aws-prod-core.
Root-cause attribution ranked the injected series first for 12 of 12 detected anomalies (100%).
Savings estimate covers 65% of the injected excess on detected anomalies ($92,693 of $142,213); 1 false-positive event(s), 1 of them on planned events.
